proposed.explanation: Critical regionalism requires genuine engagement with local values and knowledge, which this scenario lacks. Vernacular requires organic emergence from community; external design disqualifies it. The architect's origin is less significant than the depth of engagement with local context. Vernacular architecture emerges from within communities over time. A building by an outside architect using regional forms without genuine engagement with local knowledge and values is appropriation—borrowing cultural elements without understanding or respect.
